newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian kuna official in E. Slavonia from May 19.
newsitem.headline: Croatian kuna official in E. Slavonia from May 19.

text.p: The Croatian kuna will become the official currency across the whole country from May 19, when it is introduced as the only means of payment in the rebel Serb enclave of Eastern Slavonia, state television said on Monday.

While the kuna replaced the Yugoslav dinar after Croatia broke away from former Yugoslavia in 1991, the dinar is still widely used in Eastern Slavonia, which is under U.N. authority and due to revert to Zagreb's direct control in July.

State television said citizens in Eastern Slavonia with Croatian documents would be able to exchange their dinars for kuna at local post offices and some other government buildings, between May 19 and 21.
Each individual can exchange up to 2,000 dinars at any one time and the exchange rate will be determined on the day of transaction, the television quoted Crotian central bank officials as saying.

Sources close to the government have said the kuna is likely to be exchanged at a rate of one to one for the dinar, which currently trades officially at 3.3 to the German mark. The kuna is currently worth 3.57 to the mark.
